title: Putting Out Fire
description: Now you know what fire needs — use it against Lord Cinder! Learn the three ways to stop a fire and claim ember 4.

content.value: To put out a fire, you remove at least one side of the fire triangle. There are three ways to do it: remove the fuel, cut off the oxygen, or lower the temperature below the ignition point.

TO STOP A FIRE, REMOVE ONE SIDE:
🪵  remove the FUEL     → nothing left to burn
🌬️  cut off the OXYGEN  → smother the flames
💧  lower the HEAT      → cool below ignition temperature

Water is the most common fire extinguisher. It works mainly by COOLING — it lowers the temperature of the burning material below its ignition temperature. It also forms steam that helps cut off the oxygen supply.

Water is dangerous on some fires! Never use water on electrical fires (you could get an electric shock) or on oil/petrol fires (oil floats on water and the fire spreads). For these, we cut off the oxygen instead — for example with a blanket, sand, or a carbon dioxide extinguisher.
Smothering a small fire with a thick blanket or sand works by cutting off oxygen. This is also why 'stop, drop and roll' puts out clothing fires — rolling smothers the flames.
Key Takeaway: A fire is put out by removing fuel, cutting off oxygen, or cooling below the ignition temperature. Water cools fires but must never be used on electrical or oil fires.

quiz.question: Water puts out most fires mainly by…
options: cooling the burning material below its ignition temperature
quiz.explain: Water lowers the temperature below the ignition point, so the fuel can no longer burn.

quiz.question: Why should you NOT use water on an oil or petrol fire?
options: Oil floats on water, so the fire spreads
Water makes oil burn hotter forever
quiz.explain: Oil floats on water and the burning oil spreads with it, making the fire worse.

quiz.question: Smothering a fire with a blanket works by…
quiz.explain: A blanket blocks the air, cutting off oxygen — one side of the fire triangle.
